stemMd: A speaker says, “My neighbour became wealthy after buying a bicycle, so buying a bicycle is a reliable way to become wealthy.” What is the central reasoning error?

options.label: E
options.textMd: Inferring a general causal rule from one sequence of events.

explanationMd: One event occurring before another does not show that it caused it. A single case also does not establish a reliable general rule. Other factors could explain the neighbour’s wealth independently of bicycle ownership.

distractorRationale.c: No valid identity connects the events.
distractorRationale.d: The speaker relies too strongly on one observation.
distractorRationale.b: The problem is causal and generalizing, not an overly precise definition.
distractorRationale.a: Only one person’s experience is described.
